A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropy-based analysis of diffusion speciation. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture calculations, EDM2-XS and Stable Diffusion 1.5 experiments, generated examples and guidance evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds synthetic class-structure experiments, estimator-bias and convergence analyses, and an SDXL experiment in its appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the binary-entropy sign and moves final aggregation after both sampling branches. These are corrections to the stated procedure; posterior tracking, balanced priors and the unconditional-model approximation already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds covariance-separated concentric Gaussians and a hierarchical mixture combining mean and covariance distinctions, extending the synthetic scenarios beyond mean-separated components. ImageNet and the existing text-prompt tasks remain; repeating the chair experiment with SDXL changes the model setting rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: New estimator-validation comparisons use ground-truth Gaussian-mixture entropy and intermediate estimators with natural priors, true complements and exact posteriors as references (Appendix B, Figures 7–8). The original unguided, limited-guidance and full-guidance comparisons retain their comparator set.

E3.justification: New protocols include 200-component mixture tests across dimensions 2, 8, 32 and 128, an EDM2-XS sample-count sweep with 200 integration steps, and a 25K-sample prior comparison. SDXL base 1.0 is also evaluated. The original EDM2-XS and SD 1.5 sampling settings and guidance-evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds systematic tests separating bias from prior balancing, complement approximation and posterior estimation, plus dimensional sensitivity and sample convergence (Figures 7–8). Appendix C adds an SDXL robustness case study. These substantially extend v1's qualitative discussion of estimator reliability.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 8 newly reports estimator standard deviations calculated using 20 seeds. v1 contains no corresponding repeated-seed uncertainty analysis. The existing median and interquartile summaries across ImageNet classes remain; the PDFs do not establish increased repetitions of the original experiments.

E6.justification: New results show covariance-driven and two-stage hierarchical entropy transitions, quantify approximation biases and convergence, and report smoother SDXL profiles with better qualitative prompt adherence (Figures 6–8 and 18). Figure 1a's toy curves are also revised. Original guidance scores are unchanged: v1 Tables 1–2 match v2 Tables 2–3, including limited-guidance optima of FID 3.55 and FDDINOv2 87.8.

T1.justification: v2 substantially develops Appendix A with pairwise entropy-production derivations, explicit Gaussian probability bounds and partitioned-entropy identities. Sections 4.4 and A.4 extend the argument to proper/pure class decompositions and covariance-based separation. It also resolves the sign inconsistency between v1's main-text Eq. 8 and its appendix derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the theoretical contribution from detecting speciation in high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures to detecting general class-structure speciation times. Section 2 explicitly includes classes not separated by first moments. The central empirical claims about semantic timing and guidance redistribution remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds the qualification that balancing priors can alter profile shape even when the characteristic transition window remains stable, and conditions the complement approximation on representative unconditional sampling (Appendix B). It interprets the SDXL example as supporting a link between prompt adherence and diagnostic interpretability. Section 6's original limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds explicit posterior-update equations and discloses Gaussian smoothing followed by interpolation for obtaining entropy derivatives. Appendix C newly reports GPU models, batch sizes and approximate profile-computation times, including SDXL. Existing sampler, schedule and main-experiment sample counts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Achilli et al. (2026) and explicitly connects the entropy diagnostic to its general class-structure speciation framework. This extends the prior connection to Biroli et al.; the broader information-theory and guided-diffusion positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–B are extensively rewritten and reorganized around pairwise competition, score separation and estimator robustness. Implementation explanations move into Section 5.1, and Appendix C's narrative is substantially edited and reorganized. These changes extend beyond inserting new scientific material.

P2.justification: v2 adds a theory-summary table and Figures 6–8 and 18, redraws Figure 1a, reformats the guidance tables and rearranges generation montages. Three separate guidance-trajectory figures are consolidated into Figure 12, while retained Stable Diffusion examples and the failure case are relocated with expanded captions.

improvement.justification: v1 relied on largely unquantified estimator approximations and a terse asymptotic argument. v2 corrects formula and pseudocode inconsistencies, strengthens the mathematical reasoning, and directly evaluates approximation bias and convergence with repeated-seed variability. These changes substantially improve support for the diagnostic's reliability and reproducibility despite unchanged guidance scores. The general-class extension remains asymptotic, and the added SDXL evidence is qualitative.
